source_text: Ante terra aperitur in germen, quam opera colentis semen accipiat; quod in puerperio virginis approbatur, quae munere matris officium praevenit et exclusit uxoris. Quod ergo in usu non erat, id facturum se Deus omnipotens pollicetur; et addit, praevidens infidelium multitudinem: Vae qui contradicit fictori suo, testa de samiis terrae [n378] . Id est: Vae his qui, Deo promittente, fetam fieri virginem non potuisse contendunt; cumque ipsi totidem licet de seminibus a Deo institutis, tamen interveniente Dei potentia, in visceribus fingantur maternis, obstipo studio affirmant, nequivisse carnem sine ministerio viri ex carne virginis fabricari. Tale est igitur quod vos, o pervicaces, non putatis me id facere potuisse, ac mihi de rei difficultate praescribitis, cum vos ipsos manibus meis constet effectos; quale, si lutum figulo suo, cum ab eo tractatur, diceret: Non habes manus; quibus tunc in vas aliquod formabatur. Ita ergo et vos, qui inquiritis quis filium virgini dederit sine viri semine, cognoscite eumdem esse qui vos fecit ex semine. Sed iam quoniam Scripturis sanctis expositio varia licet, utraque tamen pia et religiosa concinuit, primus terminetur liber; suo tamen fine commonens, ut opifex nascentium Deus credatur, innocentium tutor, Catholicorum remunerator, Manichaeorumque damnator.
pass_a_gloss: Before is the earth opened into a shoot, than it receives seed by the works of the one cultivating; which is approved in the childbearing of the virgin, who by the gift of a mother preceded the office and shut out that of a wife. What therefore was not in use, that the omnipotent God promises that he will do; and he adds, foreseeing a multitude of the unfaithful: Woe who contradicts his fashioner, a potsherd from the Samian things of the earth. That is: Woe to these who, God promising, contend that a virgin could not become pregnant; and when they themselves, though as many from seeds instituted by God, nevertheless with the power of God intervening, are fashioned in maternal viscera, by stiff study affirm, that flesh could not have been fabricated without the ministry of a man from the flesh of a virgin. Such therefore is that you, o obstinate, do not think me to have been able to do this, and you prescribe to me from the difficulty of the thing, when it stands that you yourselves have been effected by my hands; of such a kind, if clay to its potter, when it is treated by him, would say: You have not hands; by which it was then being formed into some vessel. So therefore also you, who inquire who gave a son to a virgin without the seed of a man, know it to be the same who made you from seed. But now since to the Holy Scriptures a varied exposition is allowed, yet both pious and religious have sounded together, let the first book be ended; warning nevertheless by its own end, that God the craftsman of those being born be believed, tutor of innocents, remunerator of Catholics, and condemner of Manichaeans.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil

pass_b_english: The earth opens to bring forth a shoot before it receives seed through the cultivator's work. This is fulfilled in the Virgin's childbirth: through the gift of motherhood she preceded and excluded the function of a wife. Almighty God promises to do what was not customary. Foreseeing the multitude of unbelievers, he adds: “Woe to one who contradicts his maker, a potsherd among the earth's earthenware!” (Isaiah 45:9). That is: “Woe to those who, despite God's promise, insist that a virgin could not become pregnant! Although every one of them is shaped in a mother's womb from seeds established by God, with God's power intervening, they obstinately insist that flesh could not have been fashioned from the Virgin's flesh without a man's service” (compare Luke 1:34–35).

“You stubborn people, when you think I could not do this and prescribe limits to me because of its difficulty, although you yourselves were plainly made by my hands, you are like clay that, while being worked by its potter, said to him, ‘You have no hands’, the very hands then shaping it into a vessel. So you who ask who gave the Virgin a son without a man's seed must recognize that it is the same one who made you from seed.”

But since Holy Scripture permits varied interpretation, and both explanations have harmonized in a devout and reverent way, let the first book now end. Let its ending nevertheless remind the reader to believe that God is the maker of newborn children, the protector of the innocent, the rewarder of catholics, and the condemner of Manichaeans.

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Julian claims the catholic faith against Augustine; keep lowercase-c catholic as the universal church, not a later confessional brand.
